questions.prompt: Put these Order-to-Cash steps, per Lesson 1, in the correct order from the customer's initial decision to buy through the books being reconciled.
items: Order capture - the customer agrees to a sale in Order Management or a CRM
Fulfillment - the goods ship or the service is delivered
Invoicing - Receivables creates a transaction recording what the customer owes
Collection - the customer pays and Receivables applies the receipt
Close and reconciliation - accounting entries flow to General Ledger and the subledger is reconciled
questions.explain: Order-to-Cash always runs order capture, fulfillment, invoicing, collection, then close and reconciliation, in that order. Receivables itself only owns the invoicing and collection steps in the middle - it doesn't create the sale and it doesn't literally move money.

questions.prompt: An AR clerk completes a $9,500 standard invoice for a customer on June 1. The customer still hasn't paid by June 30. Which pair of statuses correctly describes the invoice at that point?
options: Completion status: Complete; Balance status: Open
Completion status: Incomplete; Balance status: Open
Completion status: Complete; Balance status: Closed
Completion status: Incomplete; Balance status: Closed
Completion status: Complete; Balance status: Pending
Completion status: Open; Balance status: Complete
questions.explain: Completing a transaction only answers whether it's finished being entered - it says nothing about whether it's been paid. A completed invoice can sit Open for a long time if the customer hasn't paid, which is exactly this case.

questions.prompt: Select every true statement about Receivables system options and AutoAccounting, per Chapter 1.
options: There is one system options record per business unit, not one per installation
AutoAccounting can derive different GL account segments from different sources, such as transaction type for revenue and salesperson for cost center
AutoAccounting requires every segment of every account to be typed manually by the person entering the transaction
A company with three business units transacting in Receivables needs three separate system options records
System options are typically reconfigured on every new transaction entered
questions.explain: System options are scoped per business unit, so three business units need three records. AutoAccounting builds an account segment by segment from a chosen source per segment, like transaction type or salesperson - it's the opposite of manual account entry, and system options are configured once during setup, not per transaction.

questions.prompt: Northwind Fixtures Co. offers Harborline Retail Group '2/10 Net 30' terms on a $9,000 invoice dated April 1. Harborline pays on April 9, inside the discount window. Fill in the exact dollar amount Harborline actually owes.
questions.explain: '2/10 Net 30' means 2% off if paid within 10 days, full amount due by day 30. Paying on day 9 qualifies for the discount: 2% of $9,000 is $180, so Harborline owes $9,000 minus $180, which is $8,820.

questions.prompt: Match each Trading Community Model layer to what it actually is.
right: A physical address associated with a party, independent of any selling relationship
A party site used in the context of a specific customer account, carrying one or more site uses
An organization or person that can enter into a business relationship, independent of any specific deal
Created when a party enters into a selling relationship with the business; carries payment terms and a credit profile
questions.explain: Party is identity, independent of any deal. Party site is a bare address. Customer account is the selling relationship itself, carrying business terms. Account site is a party site put to use for a specific account, carrying site uses like Bill-To and Ship-To.

questions.prompt: Harborline Retail Group buys from Northwind for two store divisions that need to age and report separately, even though both belong to the same legal entity. What is the correct way to model this in the Trading Community Model?
options: Create one party and one customer account, and track the two divisions with a free-text note
Create two separate parties, one for each division
Create one party with two customer accounts, each with its own account site carrying a Bill-To use
Create one party, one customer account, and two account sites, one flagged 'East' and one 'West'
Merge the two divisions into a single customer account using a split payment term
Create two party sites under one account, each assigned a different profile class
questions.explain: A single party can have more than one customer account. Giving each division its own account (each with its own Bill-To account site) is exactly how Receivables lets two divisions of the same real-world company age and report independently.

questions.prompt: Harborline Retail Group is assigned the 'Standard Wholesale' profile class, which sets a $50,000 credit limit. Harborline currently has $42,000 in open invoices, and a new order would create an $11,000 invoice. Select every true statement about what happens next, per Chapter 2.
options: The new invoice would push Harborline's open balance to $53,000, which exceeds the $50,000 limit
Receivables can be configured to flag the transaction for a credit hold rather than silently blocking entry
The invoice is automatically and permanently rejected, with no way to ever complete it
A credit analyst can review the account and manually release the hold without changing any system-wide setting
Because the profile class sets the limit, no individual account can ever carry a different credit limit than its profile class default
questions.explain: $42,000 plus $11,000 is $53,000, over the $50,000 limit, which can trigger a credit hold for review rather than a hard, permanent block - a credit analyst can review and release it as a one-time, documented exception. Any profile class value, including credit limit, can still be overridden on an individual account.

questions.prompt: Cascade Outdoor Supply has two separate customer accounts under the same party, and both are authorized to use the same bank account for automatic receipts. Fill in the blank: a customer bank account is associated with the ________, not a specific account site, which is exactly why it can be reused across more than one customer account belonging to that entity.
questions.explain: A customer bank account lives at the party level, similar to how a party can have multiple addresses. That's what lets the same bank account be authorized for use by more than one customer account belonging to that party.

questions.prompt: Two different Northwind business units each independently created a customer record for the same real-world company months apart. The AR team identifies the duplicate and designates the record with more transaction history as the survivor. What happens to the duplicate account's existing invoices and receipts when the merge runs?
options: They are deleted, since the duplicate account is being removed from the system
They are moved to the surviving account, preserving aging, statements, and application history
They remain on the duplicate account, which stays active alongside the surviving account
They are moved to the surviving account, but all receipt application history is reset and must be reapplied manually
They are written off as part of the merge process, since a duplicate account's balance is no longer trustworthy
They are flagged for review but left on the duplicate account until someone manually reassigns each one
questions.explain: A merge moves both transactions and their receipt applications to the surviving account, preserving the full history, and inactivates the duplicate rather than deleting it - the audit trail stays intact and nothing needs to be manually reapplied.

questions.prompt: Match each Chapter 3 setup object to what it controls.
right: Controls numbering, date derivation, and whether transactions were entered manually or imported through AutoInvoice
Defines a transaction's sign, whether it opens a receivable, and its natural application behavior
Provides default GL accounting for adjustments, miscellaneous cash, write-offs, and similar non-transaction activity
Provides a reusable description and default accounting for ad hoc charges like a debit memo or chargeback line
questions.explain: Transaction type controls sign, open-receivable behavior, and natural application. Transaction source controls numbering, date handling, and manual-versus-imported defaulting. Receivables activities default accounting for adjustments, misc cash, and write-offs. Memo lines default a description and accounting for ad hoc charges.

questions.prompt: Northwind wants 'Intercompany Invoice' and 'Standard Invoice' to behave differently - different default accounting, different printing options - but both should still increase what the customer owes and open a receivable. What's the correct way to set this up?
options: Create two different transaction classes, Intercompany Invoice and Standard Invoice
Create two different transaction types, both tied to the Invoice class, each with its own accounting and printing defaults
Create one transaction type and switch its creation sign depending on which invoice is being entered
Create two transaction sources instead, since sources are what control default accounting references
Use a single transaction type and rely on memo lines to tell the two invoice kinds apart
Create two receivables activities, one for each kind of invoice
questions.explain: Transaction class is a small, fixed set (Invoice, Credit Memo, Debit Memo, and a few others) - you cannot create new classes. Transaction type is what you define, tied to exactly one class, and a class can have several types, each with its own sign, accounting, and printing defaults.

questions.prompt: Northwind sells a 12-month maintenance contract for $12,000, invoiced in full on January 1 with Net 30 terms, using a deferred revenue scheduling rule. Select every true statement about this transaction, per Lesson 16.
options: The full $12,000 is still invoiced and due according to Net 30 terms, regardless of the revenue scheduling rule
At completion, Receivables books a debit to Accounts Receivable and a credit to Unearned Revenue for the full $12,000
Because revenue is deferred, the invoice itself isn't created until the first month's revenue is recognized
Revenue is recognized across the twelve periods, moving amounts from Unearned Revenue into Revenue as each period runs
Deferred recognition delays the Net 30 due date until enough revenue has been recognized to cover the payment
questions.explain: Revenue recognition timing is purely an accounting decision - it doesn't change invoicing or due dates. The invoice is created and due in full under Net 30 on day one; the $12,000 sits in Unearned Revenue at completion and moves to Revenue one-twelfth at a time as each period's recognition runs.

questions.prompt: A shipment arrives damaged, and Harborline is charged a $75 fee for the replacement process. Rather than typing a free-text description and picking a GL account manually, the AR clerk selects a predefined description with default accounting already attached. Fill in the blank: this reusable object is called a ________.
questions.explain: A standard memo line is a predefined line description paired with default accounting references and tax classification, used on debit memos, on-account credits, and chargebacks - exactly the ad hoc 'something happened and we need to bill for it' situation here.

questions.prompt: Put these steps of creating a Receivables invoice, per Lesson 17, in the correct order from a blank form to a completed transaction.
items: Select the transaction source, which can default the transaction type and numbering
Select or confirm the transaction type, setting the sign and whether a receivable opens
Select the customer account and bill-to site, pulling in tax and currency defaults
Confirm or override the payment terms defaulted from the customer's profile
Enter one or more lines with descriptions, quantities, and amounts
Review the distributions derived by AutoAccounting
Complete the transaction, locking header fields and making it eligible for accounting
questions.explain: Source and type are chosen first because so much else defaults from them. Customer and terms come next, then lines are entered, distributions are reviewed, and completion is the final step that locks the header and makes the invoice eligible for the Create Accounting process.

questions.prompt: A $10,000 invoice is outstanding. The customer pays only $9,200 and unilaterally deducts $800 for a damage claim the business has reviewed and rejected as unsupported, and the business still expects to collect the $800. Which transaction correctly represents how Receivables should record this?
options: A chargeback, which closes the invoice using the $9,200 payment and creates a new $800 debit item
An adjustment that writes off the $800 difference against the original invoice
A debit memo for $800 that is unrelated to the original invoice, billed as a new standalone charge
A standard credit memo for $800 applied against the original invoice
A receipt write-off for the $800 shortfall at the time of applying the $9,200 payment
An on-account credit memo for $800, to be applied toward a future invoice
questions.explain: A chargeback is specifically the response to an underpayment on an existing invoice: it closes the original invoice using the payment received plus the chargeback, and creates a brand-new debit item for the disputed, still-collectible amount.
questions.distractorExplain: Option C is the closest wrong answer, since both a chargeback and a debit memo create a new debit item for $800. The difference is what the new item is connected to: a debit memo is a standalone new charge with no link to an existing invoice, while a chargeback specifically closes an existing underpaid invoice and recreates the shortfall. Treating this as a plain debit memo would leave the original $10,000 invoice sitting open instead of properly closed against the $9,200 received.

questions.prompt: An invoice has two item lines: $8,000 of taxable fixtures and $1,500 of non-taxable installation labor, plus a flat $100 freight line. The applicable sales tax rate is 7%, and tax applies only to taxable lines. What is the total invoice amount?
options: $10,060.00 total, leaving out the freight line from the calculation
$9,600.00 total, leaving tax out of the calculation entirely
$10,160.00 total, since the 7% tax applies only to the $8,000 taxable line
$10,265.00 total, since the 7% tax applies to both the taxable and non-taxable item lines
$10,272.00 total, since the 7% tax applies to the full item-plus-freight subtotal
$9,500.00 total, counting only the two item lines with no tax or freight
questions.explain: Tax is determined by the taxable status of each line, not a flat rate on the whole invoice. 7% of the $8,000 taxable line is $560. Adding the items ($8,000 + $1,500), freight ($100), and tax ($560) gives $10,160.00.

questions.prompt: Order Management stages 400 lines in the AutoInvoice interface tables overnight, tagged to the 'OM AutoInvoice Import' source. The next morning, 397 lines became real transactions and 3 lines are sitting in an interface errors table referencing an end-dated customer site. Select every true statement about this situation, per Lesson 21.
options: The 3 failed lines were rejected during the validation phase, before grouping or transfer ever ran on them
The 3 failed lines are permanently lost and must be re-entered manually as brand-new transactions
Once the site reference is corrected, the 3 lines can be resubmitted through AutoInvoice rather than keyed manually
The 397 successful lines were created as real Receivables transactions, complete with AutoAccounting-derived distributions
Because AutoInvoice failed on 3 lines, the entire batch of 400 lines must be reprocessed from scratch
questions.explain: AutoInvoice's validation phase is where line-level problems get caught, and failed lines move to an interface errors table rather than being lost - they wait for correction and resubmission. Lines that pass get grouped and transferred into real, fully accounted transactions, and a handful of failures don't force the whole batch to be redone.

questions.prompt: Before a transaction can move from Incomplete to Complete, Receivables checks several fixed conditions. Fill in the blank: one of them is that a valid customer with a ________ site must be present.
questions.explain: Receivables cannot complete a transaction without a valid customer carrying a Bill-To site - that's the one site use Receivables cannot do without, even though Ship-To matters for tax and fulfillment linkage.

questions.prompt: Match each Chapter 5 cash term to what it actually describes.
right: Money received from a customer, applied fully or partially against one or more open transactions
Money received that isn't a payment against any customer transaction, distributed directly to GL accounts
Money matched to a known customer but not yet matched to a specific transaction
A standing credit on a customer's account, deliberately not tied to any specific invoice
questions.explain: A standard receipt applies against open transactions. A miscellaneous receipt is unrelated to any customer balance and posts straight to GL. Unapplied cash is tied to a customer but not yet matched to a transaction. On-account cash is a deliberate standing credit, not tied to any invoice.

questions.prompt: Meridian Office Supply owes $4,250.00 on an invoice but sends a check for $4,500.00, and the clerk applies $4,250.00 to close the invoice. Select every valid way Receivables allows the remaining $250.00 to be handled.
options: Leave it unapplied on the receipt, to apply toward a future invoice
Apply it on-account, associating it with the customer without tying it to any specific transaction
Refund it back to the customer if the overpayment was a genuine error
Automatically write it off as a receipt write-off, since any overpayment must be absorbed as a loss
Apply it as a positive adjustment against a different customer's invoice
questions.explain: Receivables gives three options for excess payment: leave it unapplied, put it on-account, or refund it. A receipt write-off is for a small leftover underpayment, not an overpayment, and nothing can be applied against a different customer's transaction.

questions.prompt: A collections agent works strictly off the aging report and sees Meridian Office Supply's invoice #3104 as 45 days past due, so a dunning letter goes out. It turns out Meridian has a $1,800 receipt sitting unapplied since three weeks ago that exactly covers the invoice. What does this scenario best illustrate, per Lesson 26?
options: Aging reports are driven by open invoice balances, and unapplied cash doesn't reduce that balance until it's actually applied, so relying on aging alone can trigger a false escalation
Unapplied cash automatically closes the oldest open invoice the moment it's received, so this situation should never occur
The invoice was already closed, and the dunning letter was sent because of a system error
On-account cash and unapplied cash are the same status, so the receipt should have closed the invoice automatically
Aging reports automatically net out any unapplied receipts tied to the same customer before sorting balances into buckets
The collections agent should have used a 4-bucket aging report instead of a 7-bucket one to catch this
questions.explain: Unapplied cash belongs to the customer in a practical sense, but formally every open invoice still shows its full balance until the cash is actually applied against it - which is exactly why clearing unapplied and on-account cash before trusting aging is part of good receivables hygiene.

questions.prompt: Put these stages of the automatic receipts batch process, per Lesson 27, in the correct order.
items: Create - Receivables generates the batch of receipts for every eligible transaction
Approve - someone reviews and approves the batch before it becomes final
Format - the batch is formatted into the file the bank or payment network expects
Confirm - the receipts are confirmed as real, finalizing them in Receivables
Remit - the confirmed receipts are sent to the bank for actual processing
questions.explain: Automatic receipts move through create, approve, format, confirm, and remit, in that order - a company can require a manual checkpoint at any stage or let the whole sequence run unattended.

questions.prompt: Meridian Office Supply's $4,250.00 check closes an invoice, then bounces two weeks later for non-sufficient funds. The AR clerk wants the original invoice to stay marked as paid while creating a brand-new obligation, plus an NSF fee, for the customer to pay again. Fill in the blank: this calls for a ________ reversal, not a standard reversal.
questions.explain: A standard reversal would simply reopen the original invoice. A debit memo reversal keeps the original invoice closed and instead creates a new debit memo for the reversed amount - the standard approach for an NSF check, since the business still has a real, renewed claim against the customer.

questions.prompt: A customer's $3,000 balance is confirmed accurate - they genuinely owe it - but after collections efforts are exhausted, the business decides it will never be paid and wants it removed from the books while keeping the transaction visible in history. Which action correctly matches this situation?
options: A transaction write-off, since it's correct but deemed uncollectible
A negative adjustment, since the balance needs to be corrected downward
A standard credit memo applied against the original invoice
An on-account credit memo issued to offset the balance
A receipt write-off recorded at the time of applying a partial payment
A chargeback that recreates the balance as a new transaction
questions.explain: A transaction write-off formally abandons collection of a balance everyone agrees is correct, while leaving the transaction in history for audit purposes - exactly this situation after collections has run its course.
questions.distractorExplain: Option B is the closest wrong answer, because both a negative adjustment and a write-off reduce a balance to zero through a similar-looking entry. The difference is intent: an adjustment says the number itself is wrong and corrects it, while a write-off says the number is right but the business has given up collecting it. Since the scenario states the balance is accurate and collections is exhausted, it's a write-off, not an adjustment.

questions.prompt: Select every valid Receivables Activity type used for non-transaction, non-receipt accounting in this course.
options: Adjustment
Miscellaneous Cash
Standard Invoice
Late Charges
Bill-To Site
Receipt Write-offs
questions.explain: Adjustment, Miscellaneous Cash, Late Charges, and Receipt Write-offs are all Receivables Activity types. Standard Invoice is a transaction type, not a receivables activity, and Bill-To is a site use, not an activity type at all.

questions.prompt: A company's dunning policy sends a follow-up letter every 15 days since the last letter went out, regardless of which specific invoice is oldest. Which dunning method is this, per Lesson 32?
options: Staged dunning
Aged dunning
Collections Workbench dunning
4-bucket dunning
On-account dunning
Statement-cycle dunning
questions.explain: Staged dunning bases the next letter on time since the last letter was sent, regardless of which transaction is oldest. Aged dunning, by contrast, is driven by how old the single oldest past-due transaction is.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: compared to a 7-bucket aging report, a 4-bucket aging report has ________ buckets, each covering a wider range of days past due.
questions.explain: A 4-bucket report uses four broader ranges, while a 7-bucket report slices the same balances into seven narrower ranges - which is why a 7-bucket report can tell apart a transaction barely 31 days overdue from one 89 days overdue, and a 4-bucket report can't.

questions.prompt: Select every true statement about standard Receivables accounting, per Lesson 35.
options: A standard invoice typically debits Accounts Receivable and credits Revenue
A standard receipt typically debits Cash and credits Accounts Receivable
A miscellaneous receipt debits Cash and credits Accounts Receivable, just like a standard receipt
Receivables posts directly to the General Ledger the moment a clerk saves a transaction, without going through Subledger Accounting
AutoAccounting can derive GL account segments from attributes like transaction type, Receivables Activity, or salesperson
questions.explain: An invoice debits AR and credits Revenue; a standard receipt debits Cash and credits AR. A miscellaneous receipt still debits Cash, but credits whatever GL account its Receivables Activity specifies, not Accounts Receivable, since there's no customer balance involved. Receivables is a subledger - it never posts directly to GL without Subledger Accounting translating the entries first.

questions.prompt: At period close, the Receivables to Ledger Reconciliation Report shows the GL's Accounts Receivable account balance is $4,250.00 higher than what Receivables itself shows as total open balances. Which cause, per Lesson 38's troubleshooting guidance, best fits a GL balance that is overstated relative to Receivables?
options: A manual journal entry was made directly in GL, bypassing Receivables entirely
A transaction finalized its accounting but was never transferred or posted to GL
A transaction is still sitting Incomplete and hasn't been accounted at all
A receipt was reversed using a standard reversal instead of a debit memo reversal
The reconciliation process was run using a 7-bucket aging report instead of common currency
A customer merge moved transactions from a duplicate account into the surviving account
questions.explain: An out-of-process manual journal entry made directly in GL, bypassing Receivables, inflates the GL side relative to what Receivables itself shows - exactly the kind of entry the Differences report is built to surface.

questions.prompt: Put these steps of a Receivables period close, per Lesson 38, in the correct order.
items: Finish month-end activity: import remaining billing data, apply outstanding receipts, approve pending adjustments and write-offs
Run Create Accounting for the period so nothing sits unaccounted
Set the Receivables period status to Close Pending
Run the Prepare Receivables to General Ledger Reconciliation process
Resolve any differences, then close the period for good
questions.explain: A Receivables close finishes month-end activity, runs final accounting, moves the period to Close Pending as a transitional safety step, reconciles against GL, and only then resolves any differences and closes the period for good.
